svg.title: How the Senate debates a question
svg.desc: A semicircular chamber of senators around a clerk's desk. You ask a question and pick a size from 3 to 15 senators. Round 1: every senator gives an opening view. The clerk drafts one answer. Each later round, every senator votes agree, amend, or dissent and sharpens their view. When nobody dissents and most agree, the draft passes; otherwise the clerk redrafts, up to a round limit. You get one answer, the points everyone agreed on, and any dissent, credited to the senator who raised it.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The Senate: one question, many minds, one answer
